seoDescription.en: Rizal gave this terracotta of Saint Paul of Thebes to Fr. Pablo Pastells amid their intense debate over faith, reason, and the Church's power.

title.en: San Pablo El Ermitano, Dedicated to Fr. Pablo Pastells, S.J.

description.en:
Between 1892 and 1893, Rizal exchanged letters with Fr. Pablo Pastells, who wanted to win Rizal back to the Catholic faith after Rizal exposed the Church’s abuse of power in his writings and was excommunicated after joining the freemasons. Rizal gave Fr. Pastells a terracotta sculpture of San Pablo el Ermitano or Saint Paul of Thebes who fled from Roman persecution and became the first Christian hermit in Catholic Church history. On February 2, 1893, Fr. Pastells acknowledged the gift and took it as though Rizal’s heart had remained Christian, despite his rebellious ideas. Rizal replied that Fr. Pastells should not consider his art work an unconscious confession and that creative expression does not equate to belief. Rather, his sculpture reflects his respect for others’ faith without subscribing to it himself.

In creating this statuette, Rizal used sap from the bakhaw tree as a binder for the palm tree leaves' tunic of St. Paul. The piece is currently exhibited in the Rizal Gallery of the National Museum of Fine Arts.

## References

“Misyon ng mga Hesuwitas sa Pilipinas.” Letter to Dr. Rizal. 2 February 1893. Typescript, National Historical Commission of the Philippines.

Palma, Celestino. Jose Rizal, Sculptor. Reyes Publishing, 2020.
description.fil:
Sa pagitan ng 1892 at 1893, nagpalitan ng mga liham sina Rizal at Padre Pablo Pastells, na nagnanais na maibalik si Rizal sa pananampalatayang Katoliko matapos ibunyag ni Rizal ang pang-aabuso sa kapangyarihan ng Simbahan sa kanyang mga akda at matiwalag matapos sumapi sa mga freemason. Ibinigay ni Rizal kay Padre Pastells ang isang eskulturang terracotta ni San Pablo el Ermitano o San Pablo ng Thebes, na tumakas mula sa pag-uusig ng mga Romano at naging unang Kristiyanong ermitanyo sa kasaysayan ng Simbahang Katoliko. Noong ika-2 ng Pebrero 1893, kinilala ni Padre Pastells ang handog at itinuring itong parang nanatiling Kristiyano ang puso ni Rizal, sa kabila ng kanyang mga mapaghimagsik na kaisipan. Tumugon si Rizal na hindi dapat ituring ni Padre Pastells ang kanyang likhang sining bilang isang di-sinasadyang pagtatapat at na ang malikhaing pagpapahayag ay hindi katumbas ng pananalig. Sa halip, sumasalamin ang kanyang eskultura sa paggalang niya sa pananampalataya ng iba nang hindi niya ito sinasapi.

Sa paggawa ng estatwilyang ito, gumamit si Rizal ng dagta mula sa punong bakhaw bilang pampatibay sa tunikang dahon ng palma ni San Pablo. Nakatanghal sa kasalukuyan ang piyesa sa Rizal Gallery ng National Museum of Fine Arts.

## Mga Sanggunian

“Misyon ng mga Hesuwitas sa Pilipinas.”

Letter to Dr. Rizal. 2 February 1893. Typescript, National Historical Commission of the Philippines.

Palma, Celestino. Jose Rizal, Sculptor. Reyes Publishing, 2020.
description.de:
Zwischen 1892 und 1893 tauschten Rizal und Pater Pablo Pastells Briefe aus; Pastells wollte Rizal für den katholischen Glauben zurückgewinnen, nachdem Rizal in seinen Schriften den Machtmissbrauch der Kirche offengelegt und sich nach seinem Beitritt zu den Freimaurern die Exkommunikation zugezogen hatte. Rizal schenkte Pater Pastells eine Terrakottaskulptur des San Pablo el Ermitano, des heiligen Paulus von Theben, der der römischen Verfolgung entfloh und zum ersten christlichen Eremiten der katholischen Kirchengeschichte wurde. Am 2. Februar 1893 bestätigte Pater Pastells den Empfang des Geschenks und nahm es so auf, als sei Rizals Herz trotz seiner rebellischen Ideen christlich geblieben. Rizal erwiderte, Pater Pastells solle sein Kunstwerk nicht als unbewusstes Bekenntnis betrachten; schöpferischer Ausdruck sei nicht gleichbedeutend mit Glauben. Seine Skulptur bringe vielmehr seinen Respekt vor dem Glauben anderer zum Ausdruck, ohne dass er diesen selbst annehme.

Für diese Statuette verwendete Rizal Harz des Bakhaw-Baumes als Bindemittel für die Tunika des heiligen Paulus aus Palmblättern. Das Stück ist derzeit in der Rizal-Galerie des National Museum of Fine Arts ausgestellt.

## Literatur

“Misyon ng mga Hesuwitas sa Pilipinas.”

Letter to Dr. Rizal. 2 February 1893. Typescript, National Historical Commission of the Philippines.
